transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
Hundreds of people rallied in Ithaca, New York, Sunday in support of a former Cornell University student known as Jane Doe.
The woman says she was raped by several fraternity members at an on-campus party in 2024.
Celia Clark with member station WSKG reports.
We believe you, Jane Doe.
People held signs saying essays are not punishment for rape, and we are Jane Doe.
Elliot Larson is a student at neighboring Ithaca College and one of the rally's organizers.
They say it's all for Jane Doe.
I feel like it's really important for her to see that her community is standing with her and we're standing behind her
and we don't accept the mishandling of her case by Cornell.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul sent a message that was read at the rally reiterating her commitment to change state laws on sexual assault and consent.
More public protests in Ithaca are scheduled over the next few weeks.
For NPR News, I'm Celia Clark in Ithaca.
Brazil's presidential election is heading to a run-off vote, neither the left-wing president Luis Inacia Lula da Silva or his right-wing challenger Flavia Bolsonaro won a majority in Sunday's election.
After the vote this weekend, Bolsonaro says he's confident that Brazil will choose what he calls a modern government.
What I have to say is that Lula is fighting for power.
He has already contested seven presidential elections.
Seven presidential elections.
He cares about power.
I care about Brazil's future.
The run-off voting will take place on October 25th.
There's less than one month to go before the 2026 midterm elections and as NPR's Domenico Montanero reports,
the political landscape appears to be changing more in favor of Democrats.
History isn't kind to the president's party in midterm elections and this year is shaping up to be no different.
Negative views of the economy and the Iran war have created a tough environment for swing district Republicans.
Democrats are the favorites to pick up control of the House and the Senate appears to be within reach.
That isn't something that was thought possible at the beginning of the cycle.
But while Democrats are in the driver's seat, there are lots of reasons for why their gains may be limited.
Redistricting has helped insulate Republicans to an extent.
Most of the districts that are competitive are in places Trump won in 2024 and the Democratic Party remains unpopular.
Domenico Montanero, NPR News, Washington.
Asian stocks made strong gains on Monday as investors reduced their expectations that the Federal Reserve could hike interest rates this month.
Japan's Nikkei index rose 2 percent.
Trading, though, was thin with holidays in China and South Korea.
Oil prices edged lower with Brent crude down by half a percent and U.S. crude prices falling nine-tenths of a percent.
This is NPR News.
A U.S. Marine has been arrested in Okinawa and is being held on suspicion of killing and robbing a local woman.
Police say security camera footage shows the Marine entering the 39-year-old woman's hotel with her and later leaving alone.
Police say the victim appeared to have been strangled.
The Supreme Court opens its new term Monday and it's set to hear a landmark climate change case from the city and county of Boulder.
Colorado Public Radio's Ishaan Takur has more.
In 2018, Boulder sued the oil company's Exxon and Suncor for damages.
The suit alleges that they lied about the dangers of burning fossil fuels and should now pitch in to pay for climate-driven disasters.
Michael Girard is with the Saban Center for Climate Change Law.
They're not seeking an order that emissions be reduced or that less oil and gas and coal be mined or drilled.
They're not seeking emissions regulations. They're just seeking money damages.
The Supreme Court will not rule on the case's merits.
Instead, it's questioning whether Boulder's claims are trumped by federal law, like the Clean Air Act.
A broad ruling by the court could hamper Boulder's case and more than two dozen similar climate accountability suits nationwide.
For NPR News, I'm Ishaan Takur in Boulder.
The new film starring Tom Cruise bombed at the box office this weekend.
The satire Digger was panned by critics and brought in just $8 million in ticket sales.
Instead, the erotic psychological thriller Verity debuted in first with $32.5 million from North American theaters.
The latest in the Resident Evil horror flicks showed staying power, finishing in second, adding $12.5 million to its gross.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
Want to hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?

That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Hundreds rally in Ithaca, New York supporting Cornell student who says she was raped by fraternity members
Brazil's presidential election heads to runoff between leftist Lula and rightist Bolsonaro after Sunday voting
Democrats favored to gain House control and make Senate gains ahead of 2026 midterm elections
Asian stocks rise as investors reduce expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month
U.S. Marine arrested in Okinawa on suspicion of killing and robbing local 39-year-old woman
Supreme Court to hear climate case from Boulder, Colorado against oil companies Exxon and Suncor
Tom Cruise film Digger bombs at box office with $8 million, thriller Verity debuts first
